sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in the matter, has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. FIR in Crime No.53/2023 was registered by Mudbi police station, Bidar against the petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 23.08.2023 received from respondent No.2, who is the mother of the victim girl aged 16 years.
During the course of investigation of the case, petitioner herein was arrested on 23.08.2023 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
The bail application filed by the petitioner before the trial Court in Crl.Misc.No.5227/2024 was rejected on 12.11.2024.
Therefore, petitioner is before this Court.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is a youngster aged about 23 years having no criminal antecedents.
Petitioner and victim girl were in NC: 2025:KHC-K:61 love with each other.
Petitioner is in custody for the last more than 16 months.
The Trial in the case is yet to commence, since Special Public Prosecutor has not been appointed in this case till date.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the petition.
She submits that, the petitioner is the biological father of the conception of abortus, forwarded for DNA test report.
In the event, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he is likely to tamper with the prosecution witnesses.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
6.
The FIR in the present case has been registered against the petitioner on the basis of the first information submitted by the mother of the victim girl aged 16 years.

In the first information dated 23.08.2023, it is averred that, since the victim girl was complaining of stomach pain, she was taken to the Hospital and after her medical examination, the Medical Officer had informed the first NC:
2025:KHC-K:61 informant that the victim girl was pregnant by two months.
On enquiry, the victim girl allegedly informed the first informant that the petitioner was the cause for her pregnancy and he had sexual intercourse with her against her wish by threatening her.
The petitioner aged about 23 years, having no other criminal antecedents, is arrested in the present case on 23.08.2023.
The investigation is completed and charge-sheet is filed.

The order-sheet of the trial Court would reflect that, though the charge was framed in the present case on 27.05.2024 itself, the trial in the case is not commenced, because the Special Public Prosecutor has not been appointed.

From 27.05.2024 onwards, the matter has been adjourned on nine dates for the purpose of fixing the date for trial and continuous reminders are being issued by the trial Court to the Home Secretary of the State of Karnataka to appoint a Special Public Prosecutor to conduct the cases filed under POCSO Act.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh Vs. State of Maharashtra and NC:
2025:KHC-K:61 another, reported in (2024) 9 SCC 813, wherein, at paragraph No.17, it is observed as under:
"17.

entities.text:
Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh Vs. State of Maharashtra and NC:
2025:KHC-K:61 another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the State or any prosecuting agency including the court concerned has no wherewithal to provide or protect the fundamental right of an accused to have a speedy trial as enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution then the State or any other prosecuting agency should not oppose the plea for bail on the ground that the crime committed is serious.

Article 21 of the Constitution applies irrespective of the nature of the crime."
7.
The prosecution in the present case has cited altogether 33 charge-sheet witnesses.

The petitioner who has no criminal antecedents is in the custody for last more than 16 months and the trial in the case is not yet commenced for the reason that the State has failed to appoint a Special Public Prosecutor to conduct the trial.
Therefore the chances of the trial being concluded in the near soon and the case being disposed of on merits is very remote.
8. Under these circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has made out prima facie case for grant NC: 2025:KHC-K:61 of regular bail.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order:
